title: Restore the initial value fallback errors
summary: Multi-chain sampling with unsupported initial values now reaches the intended ArgumentError. Moving @nospecialize into the method body lets Julia define the two fallback methods.

blocks.text: When someone starts several sampling chains with an unsupported initial value, the library should explain what input is required. Two error-handling methods were missing because of an annotation placed around their definitions. This PR puts the annotation inside each method. The same invalid call then gets the intended input error.

blocks.text: The PR body links Julia issue 49512. In the old syntax, @nospecialize consumes the function definition rather than defining the fallback method. The PR writes each fallback as a function and puts a bare @nospecialize inside its body.

The Nothing methods accept the default value. The AbstractArray methods check length against nchains. Other input types select the restored fallback, which throws an ArgumentError naming initial_params or initial_state. These are validators for the ensemble sample methods.

blocks.title: Public call used for the state case
blocks.code:
using AbstractMCMC, Random
struct ProbeModel <: AbstractMCMC.AbstractModel end
struct ProbeSampler <: AbstractMCMC.AbstractSampler end
sample(MersenneTwister(42), ProbeModel(), ProbeSampler(),
       MCMCSerial(), 3, 4; progress=false, initial_state=10)

blocks.title: Unsupported initial_state = 10
blocks.before: Base 418afe0: MethodError from check_initial_state(::Int64, ::Int64). The generic fallback method is absent.
blocks.after: Head 3aac86b: ArgumentError: initial_state must be specified as a vector of length equal to the number of chains or `nothing`. The generic fallback method exists.

blocks.text: The probe made the same calls with MCMCSerial(), MCMCThreads() and MCMCDistributed(). It also passed initial_params=(a=1.0, b=2.0) with the default initial_state. All six calls produced MethodError on base and ArgumentError on head. No sampler step ran in these invalid-input cases.

blocks.title: The initial_state rejection path at head
blocks.text: This selected source path follows the running example with an explicit RNG and MCMCSerial(). The initial_params check returns first because its value is nothing. An integer initial_state selects the restored generic fallback. MCMCThreads and MCMCDistributed call the same validators.

nodes.label: state fallback
nodes.text: Restored generic method. Nothing and AbstractArray have more specific methods. The generic method throws an error for other input types.

nodes.label: ArgumentError
nodes.text: The fallback error states which keyword must be an array with one value per chain or nothing. The literal message says vector.

sections.title: The patch and a useful next check

blocks.title: Move the annotation inside the fallback
blocks.text: This is the PR's change to the initial_params fallback. The initial_state fallback changes in the same way. The existing public-API probe covers both names.
The current title and short body explain the change and link its cause. A shorter replacement would add little here.

blocks.title: Check that the intended fallback still runs
blocks.text: A small compatibility check tied to the public API.
blocks.instructions: Run examples/abstractmcmc-222.jl in environments containing the exact base and head. Check unsupported initial_state and initial_params with the three default ensemble modes. Confirm that invalid inputs fail before a sampler step runs and that the serial controls still sample. Report Julia and package revisions. Do not infer performance changes from @nospecialize placement.

blocks.title: The intended error replaces the missing-method error
blocks.text: Julia 1.10.12 executed the public API on the exact base and head. hasmethod also reported no matching fallback for the probe input types on base and a matching fallback on head. The public calls establish the error change for these concrete inputs. The diagram records source relationships.

blocks.title: Both revisions passed the focused probe
blocks.text: Each revision passed 12 invalid-input assertions and 5 serial controls. The controls rejected short arrays and sampled with default nothing, a matching initial_params array, and a matching initial_state array. Both runs used the same resolved dependency manifest, two Julia threads and one process. The portable probe is examples/abstractmcmc-222.jl. The recorded results and evidence fingerprints are in examples/evidence.json.

blocks.title: The HTML works offline
blocks.text: Opened the generated file in Chrome with the page context offline. The diagram rendered without an HTTP request or page error. Zoom, keyboard and drag pan, fit, all node selectors, source-link targets, disclosures and JSON export worked. The exported JSON matched the input. A 390-pixel viewport had no page overflow.

blocks.title: Revisions, source coverage and reproduction
blocks.text:
The PR API base is 418afe0df723635aa6c228eb7b12c09a849c8380. The head is 3aac86be81ea389a3c03e15a3b601c4b67884bcf. git merge-base returned the same base. Comparisons and runtime checks use this pair.

Read the PR title, body, all issue comments, the approval review, the empty inline review list, Julia issue 49512 and its comments. Searched src, test and docs for both validators and initial-value consumers. Checked all three default ensemble callers, the unchanged Nothing and AbstractArray methods, and the single-chain step interface.

Run REVIEW_REVISION=base julia --startup-file=no --threads=2 --project=/path/to/base-env examples/abstractmcmc-222.jl and repeat with head for both values. Use environments containing the respective exact package checkouts. The reviewed package version was 5.17.0. The recorded manifest fingerprint is in examples/evidence.json.

blocks.title: Checks outside this focused explanation
blocks.text: The full package suite, downstream packages, alternate Julia versions and actual multi-process sampling were not run. Invalid distributed inputs fail before worker sampling starts. No performance claim or additional defect is established by this document.
The PR is merged at the metadata snapshot. On November 3, the maintainer said a patch release would follow fixes to CI on main. This review does not check release status.
